explanation: An evil king of Judah who reigned for 55 years and did what was evil in the Lord's sight, including practicing idolatry and sorcery.
Manasseh's son who succeeded him as king of Judah and continued to do what was evil in the Lord's sight.
King of Israel whom Manasseh was compared to because of his wickedness and idolatry.
An ancient empire and people from Mesopotamia who invaded and conquered parts of Israel and Judah. Manasseh was taken captive and led away to Babylon by the Assyrians.
An ancient city and kingdom in Mesopotamia where Manasseh was held as a prisoner.
The feeling of sorrow and regret over past actions. Manasseh repented of his sins and prayed to God for forgiveness while he was in captivity.
God's grace and mercy toward those who repent of their sins and seek reconciliation. Manasseh was forgiven and restored as king after he repented.
The process of changing or improving something. Manasseh carried out a reformation in Judah by removing idols and restoring the worship of the Lord.
